newsitem.title: TURKEY: Istanbul gold tumbles with world price.
newsitem.headline: Istanbul gold tumbles with world price.

text.p: Istanbul gold prices tumbled on Friday following fresh lows in London.
Volume eased although traders bought to take up positions against a short-term recovery, dealers said.
Gold closed sharply lower at $325.00 an ounce and 1,568,000 lira per gram, from $334.00 and 1,599,000 lira on Thursday after a 11-1/2 year low in the London market.

"Demand came from the Grand Bazaar due to the lower prices. In the medium term, prices could fall even further, but dealers expect a recovery in the short term, so there was also a lot of position taking on such expectations," one dealer said.
Turkey's unregulated gold market is centred around Istanbul's Grand Bazaar.
Volume eased to 1,250 kilos on Friday from Thursday's 1,405. With the closure of U.S. markets, banks did not conduct arbitrage deals, which usually account for higher volumes.
The Turkish currency eased to 150,200 lira against the dollar, from Wednesday's close of 149,400 lira.
Most of the day's trade -- 953 kilos -- took place in the morning session, with 79.4 percent of the total volume conducted in lira terms.
